title: Älplermagronen (Alpine macaroni with potatoes, cheese and apple sauce)

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes, cut into 1.5 cm cubes

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the potato cubes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the macaroni to the same pot and cook for another 8 to 9 minutes, until both pasta and potato are tender. Drain.
While they cook, melt the butter in a frying pan and fry the onions slowly for 15 to 20 minutes until deep golden and sweet.
Return the drained pasta and potatoes to the pot, pour in the cream and heat gently.
Stir in the grated cheese a handful at a time until melted and creamy and season with salt, pepper and a little nutmeg.
Spoon onto plates, top with the fried onions and serve with apple sauce on the side.

title: Basler Läckerli (Basel honey and spice biscuits)

ingredients.name: candied orange and lemon peel, finely chopped
icing sugar, mixed with 2 tbsp water, for glazing

steps: Warm the honey and sugar in a small saucepan until the sugar dissolves, then let it cool slightly.
Mix the flour, nuts, candied peel, spices and baking powder in a bowl.
Pour in the honey mixture and the kirsch and stir to a firm, sticky dough. Cover and chill for at least 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Roll the dough out between sheets of baking paper to about 1 cm thick and place on a tray.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until golden.
Brush the sugar glaze over the hot slab straight away, then cut into rectangles while still warm. Cool completely and store in a tin.

title: Berner Platte (Bernese platter of pork, sausages, sauerkraut and beans)

ingredients.name: smoked pork collar or thick smoked pork chops
thick slab bacon, in one piece
cooked white or borlotti beans, drained

steps: Soften the onion in the lard in a large pot, add the sauerkraut, juniper, bay leaves and wine, cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
In a separate pan, cover the smoked pork and bacon with water, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for about 1 hour 15 minutes until tender, skimming as needed.
Add the sausages to the pan for the final 15 minutes.
Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 20 minutes until tender.
Warm the beans in a little of the meat cooking liquid and season with pepper.
Slice the meats and arrange them on a large warm platter on a bed of sauerkraut, with the potatoes and beans around the edges.

title: Bircher muesli (Swiss soaked oats with grated apple)
steps: Stir the oats with the milk in a bowl, cover and chill overnight until soft.
In the morning, toss the grated apples with the lemon juice so they do not brown.
Fold the apples, yogurt and honey into the soaked oats.
Spoon into bowls and top with the nuts and berries.
Serve cold, adding a splash more milk if you like it looser.

title: Birnbrot (Swiss pear bread with a dried-fruit filling)
steps: Soak the pears, raisins and figs with the kirsch and 100 ml hot water overnight.
Mix the soaked fruit with the walnuts and spices to make the filling.
Knead the flour, yeast, milk, butter, salt and sugar into a smooth dough, cover and let it rise for 1 hour.
Roll out the dough to a rectangle about 1 cm thick and spread the filling over it, leaving a border.
Roll up the dough as for a Swiss roll, pinch the ends shut and place seam side down on a lined tray.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C. Prick the top, brush with milk and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until deep golden. Cool before slicing.

title: Bündner Nusstorte (Graubünden caramel walnut tart)
steps: Rub the butter into the flour, icing sugar and salt until crumbly, then mix in the egg to form a dough. Wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Melt the sugar in a heavy saucepan over medium heat without stirring until it becomes a golden caramel.
Carefully pour in the cream, which will bubble up, and stir until the caramel is smooth again. Add the honey.
Stir in the walnuts and let the filling cool to lukewarm.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C. Roll out two-thirds of the dough and line a 24 cm tin, trimming the edges.
Pour in the filling. Roll out the remaining dough, cover the filling, seal the edges and prick the top with a fork.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden. Cool completely before cutting.

title: Capuns (chard parcels with a spätzle-style dough)

ingredients.name: smoked bacon or air-dried beef, finely diced

steps: Whisk the flour, eggs and milk into a thick batter and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Stir in the diced meat, herbs and garlic.
Blanch the chard leaves in boiling water for 30 seconds, then drain and spread on a cloth. Trim the thick stems flat.
Put a heaped spoonful of batter on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up into a tight parcel.
Lay the parcels in a buttered baking dish in a single layer, seam side down.
Heat the stock and cream together, pour over the parcels and sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake at 180 degrees C for 30 to 35 minutes until the dough is set and the top is golden.

title: Carac (Swiss chocolate ganache tartlet with green icing)
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and 60 g icing sugar until it looks like fine crumbs. Add the yolk and enough water to bring it together, then chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C. Roll out the pastry and line four 10 cm tartlet tins, prick the bases and bake blind for 15 minutes until crisp and golden. Cool.
Heat the cream until just steaming, pour it over the chopped chocolate and stir until smooth and glossy to make the ganache. Cool until thick but still spreadable.
Fill the tartlet cases with the ganache and smooth the surfaces. Chill until firm.
Mix the remaining icing sugar with enough water to make a thick glaze and tint it a pale green.
Spread a thin layer of icing over each tartlet and let it set before serving.

title: Chäswähe (Swiss cheese tart)
steps: Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Roll out the pastry to line a 26 cm tart tin and prick the base.
Scatter most of the cheese over the pastry in an even layer.
Whisk the cream, eggs, flour, nutmeg, salt and pepper together and pour over the cheese.
Sprinkle the last of the cheese on top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until set and golden brown. Serve warm with a green salad.

title: Cholera (Valais potato, apple and cheese pie)
steps: Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Parboil the potato slices in salted water for 4 minutes and drain.
Soften the leeks and onion in the butter for 8 minutes and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Roll out half the pastry and line a 24 cm pie dish or springform tin.
Layer in half the potatoes, then the leek mixture, apples, pears and cheese, finishing with the rest of the potatoes.
Roll out the remaining pastry, cover the filling, seal and crimp the edges and cut a small steam hole in the centre.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until golden. Serve warm.

title: Cordon bleu (cheese and ham filled breaded cutlet)

ingredients.name: thin pork or veal cutlets, about 150 g each
lemon wedges and fries or potato salad

steps: Pound each cutlet thin between sheets of cling film, keeping the meat intact, then season with salt and pepper.
Place a slice of ham and a slice of cheese on one half of each cutlet, keeping them away from the edges, and fold the meat over to form a pocket. Press the edges firmly and secure with toothpicks.
Dredge each parcel in flour, dip in egg and press into breadcrumbs, shaking off the excess.
Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the cordon bleu for 5 to 6 minutes on each side until deep golden and cooked through, with the cheese melted.
Drain briefly, remove the toothpicks and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Magenbrot (glazed spiced gingerbread pieces)
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, spices, cocoa, hazelnuts and candied peel in a large bowl.
Warm the honey, 100 g sugar and milk in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves, then pour into the dry ingredients and knead to a stiff dough. Rest it for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C. Shape the dough into 3 long rolls about 3 cm thick, place on a lined tray and flatten slightly.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until firm. Cool for 10 minutes and cut each roll into 1 cm slices.
Boil the glaze sugar, water and cocoa together for about 3 minutes until syrupy.
Toss the slices in the glaze until coated, spread them out on a rack and leave to dry for a few hours until the glaze is dull and set.

title: Malakoff (fried cheese sticks from Vaud)

ingredients.name: Gruyère, cut into 8 sticks about 8 cm long
butter or oil, for shallow frying

steps: Whisk the flour, egg, wine, nutmeg and salt into a thick, smooth batter and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Dip the cheese sticks one at a time into the batter and turn to coat all sides evenly.
Melt the butter in a frying pan until sizzling over medium heat.
Lower in the battered sticks and fry for about 2 minutes per side until golden and crisp, taking care that the cheese begins to soften but does not leak out.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot with pickled onions and bread.

title: Maluns (crumbled fried potatoes with apple sauce)

ingredients.name: potatoes, boiled in their skins the day before and chilled
warm apple sauce and mountain cheese

steps: Peel the cold boiled potatoes and grate them coarsely into a bowl.
Toss the potato with the flour and salt until the shreds are coated.
Melt a third of the butter in a large heavy frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add the potato mixture and cook very slowly, turning and breaking it up with a spatula, for 30 to 40 minutes.
Add the remaining butter in two or three portions as the mixture dries out, until it forms small golden, crisp crumbs and little balls.
Serve hot with apple sauce and cheese.

title: Papet Vaudois (leek and potato stew with sausage)

ingredients.name: leeks, white and pale green parts, sliced
potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Melt the butter in a heavy casserole and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the leeks and cook gently, stirring, for 10 minutes until they collapse.
Pour in the wine and let it reduce by half, then add the stock and potatoes.
Cover and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes begin to break down and the stew is creamy.
Lay the sausages on top for the last 20 minutes so they steam in the vegetables.
Mash lightly with a spoon, season with salt, pepper and nutmeg and serve the stew with the sausages on top.

title: Raclette (melted cheese with potatoes and pickles)

ingredients.name: raclette cheese, cut into slices about 5 mm thick

steps: Scrub the potatoes and boil them in salted water in their skins for 20 to 25 minutes until tender. Drain and keep them warm in a cloth-lined bowl.
Arrange the pickles and onions in small bowls and put the pepper and paprika on the table.
Heat a raclette grill or a broiler. Put a slice of cheese in each small pan and slide it under the heat for a few minutes until bubbling and flecked with brown at the edges.
If you do not have a raclette grill, lay the cheese slices on a heatproof dish and place under a hot oven grill until molten.
Scrape the melted cheese over the potatoes on each plate, season with pepper and paprika and eat with the pickles.
Repeat with fresh slices of cheese for as long as people are hungry.

title: Risotto alla ticinese (Ticino-style risotto with sausage and red wine)

ingredients.name: fresh Italian pork sausage, skin removed and crumbled

steps: Melt half the butter in a wide, heavy pan and fry the onion gently for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the crumbled sausage and brown it for 5 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the rice and cook for 1 minute until glossy.
Pour in the red wine and stir until it has been absorbed.
Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring often, waiting until each addition is mostly absorbed. This takes about 18 to 20 minutes, until the rice is tender with a slight bite.
Stir in the remaining butter and Parmesan, season and rest for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Riz Casimir (curried chicken with fruit and rice)

ingredients.name: tinned pineapple rings, cut into pieces

steps: Cook the rice in lightly salted water according to the packet instructions, drain and keep warm.
Melt the butter in a large pan and fry the chicken strips for 4 to 5 minutes until just coloured. Remove and keep aside.
Fry the onion in the same pan for 4 minutes, stir in the curry powder and cook for 1 minute.
Add the stock and cream and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return the chicken to the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Fold in the banana, pineapple and cherries and warm through for 2 minutes.
Serve the curry over the rice, sprinkled with toasted almonds.

title: St. Galler Bratwurst with onion sauce

ingredients.name: St. Galler veal bratwurst (or other mild white sausages)

steps: Melt half the butter in a frying pan and cook the onions slowly for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then add the beer and stock, stirring, until the gravy thickens. Simmer for 10 minutes and season.
Heat a separate pan over medium heat with the remaining butter and add the sausages. Do not prick them.
Cook them for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides and cooked through.
Serve the sausages with the onion sauce poured over, with rösti or bread and mustard.

title: Zimtsterne (cinnamon star biscuits)
steps: Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, gradually adding the icing sugar and lemon juice, until thick and glossy.
Set aside about 4 tablespoons of the meringue for the topping.
Fold the cinnamon and ground almonds into the remaining meringue to make a soft dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 150 degrees C. Roll out the dough between sheets of baking paper dusted with icing sugar to about 1 cm thick.
Cut out stars with a cutter dipped in icing sugar and place on a lined tray. Brush each star with the reserved meringue.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the tops are set but the biscuits remain soft inside. Cool on a rack.

title: Zopf (Swiss braided Sunday bread)

ingredients.name: egg yolks, beaten with 1 tbsp milk, for glazing

steps: Mix the flour, salt, yeast and sugar in a large bowl.
Add the warm milk and soft butter and knead for 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour 15 minutes until doubled.
Divide the dough into 2 pieces, one about two-thirds of the weight of the other. Divide each into 3 equal ropes.
Braid the three larger ropes into a plait and set it on a lined tray. Braid the smaller ones and rest them on top, pressing gently so they stay in place.
Cover and let rise for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 200 degrees C.
Brush generously with the yolk glaze and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deeply golden, covering with foil if it browns too quickly. Cool on a rack.

title: Zuger Kirschtorte (Zug kirsch cream cake with nut meringue layers)
steps: Heat the oven to 150 degrees C. Whisk the 4 egg whites with the 100 g sugar to stiff peaks, then fold in the ground nuts and 20 g flour. Spread into two 20 cm discs on lined trays and bake for 40 to 50 minutes until dry and pale golden. Cool.
For the sponge, whisk the 3 whole eggs and 90 g sugar until thick and pale. Fold in the 90 g flour and bake in a 20 cm tin at 180 degrees C for 20 to 25 minutes. Cool and slice off any dome.
Make the custard by heating the milk, whisking the yolks, 60 g sugar and cornflour together, pouring the hot milk over and cooking the mixture until thick. Cool it completely.
Beat the soft butter until fluffy and gradually beat in the cold custard, then add 1 tablespoon of kirsch to make the buttercream.
Boil the 60 g sugar with the water, cool, and stir in 3 tablespoons of kirsch to make the syrup.
Place one meringue disc on a plate and spread with a third of the buttercream. Top with the sponge, soak it with the syrup and spread with a third more buttercream.
Add the second meringue disc, then coat the top and sides with the remaining buttercream. Press the toasted almonds on the sides and dust the top with icing sugar. Chill for at least 3 hours.

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (Zurich sliced veal in cream and mushroom sauce)

ingredients.name: veal escalopes, cut into thin strips (or pork or chicken)

steps: Pat the meat dry and toss with the flour, salt and pepper.
Melt half the butter in a large frying pan over high heat and sear the meat in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes each until just coloured. Remove to a plate.
Add the rest of the butter and fry the mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden, then add the onion and cook for 2 minutes more.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble until almost evaporated.
Add the cream and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return the meat and its juices to the pan, warm through for 1 minute without boiling, then stir in the lemon juice and parsley.
Serve immediately with rösti or noodles.

title: Zwetschgenwähe (Swiss plum tart)
steps: Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Roll out the pastry to line a 28 cm tin, prick the base and sprinkle with the ground almonds.
Arrange the plum halves in tight circles, cut side up, over the almonds.
Sprinkle the 2 tablespoons of sugar and half the cinnamon over the fruit.
Bake for 20 minutes. Meanwhile whisk the cream, egg, 1 tablespoon sugar and remaining cinnamon together.
Pour the custard around the plums and return to the oven for 15 to 20 minutes until set and the pastry is golden.
Serve warm or cool.
